name: New Chitose Airport
before:
The main airport for Sapporo and the largest in Hokkaido, about 5 km south south east of Chitose. It carried 23.7 million passengers in 2018 and was fifth busiest in Japan.

The train is quick and very busy. New Chitose Airport Station reaches Sapporo in 37 minutes on the Rapid Airport service and Otaru in 73. Trains to Sapporo are described as seriously crowded because of rising passenger numbers, so a client with heavy luggage may prefer the bus.

The Sapporo to Tokyo Haneda route is the second busiest air route in the world, carrying 12.1 million passengers in 2025.

It is one of six 24-hour airports in Japan and the only inland one, though the terminal itself has daily opening hours, so a late arrival does not mean the building is open all night.

Winter is the operational risk. The adjacent Chitose Air Base has its own runways connected by taxiways, and those are occasionally used to relieve closures here caused by winter weather.

Skytrax ranked it 49th in the world in 2024, up from 102nd, and named it the world's most improved airport that year.
after:
The main airport for Sapporo and Hokkaido, about 5 km south south east of Chitose. It handled 26.0 million passengers in the year to March 2026.

New Chitose Airport Station reaches Sapporo in about half an hour and Otaru in 73 minutes at best. JR Hokkaido warns that unreserved seats may be full, so a client with heavy luggage may prefer the direct bus into Sapporo.

On OAG's count of seats, Sapporo to Tokyo Haneda is the second busiest air route in the world, with 12.1 million seats in 2025.

It is a 24-hour airport, but the terminals close at night. The airport opens them at 5am, closes them at 11.30pm (domestic) or 9pm (international) and says no one may sleep inside after closing, except in its hotels.

Skytrax ranked it 35th in the world for 2026 (42nd in 2025) and named it the world's most improved airport in 2024.

claims.note: Was '23.7 million passengers in 2018'. For the 2025 financial year (April 2025 to March 2026) the operator's preliminary count is 26,015,370 and MLIT's sheet has 26,023,467; both give 21,487,467 domestic passengers, which ties MLIT's row to New Chitose. The operator's calendar-year table (from MLIT's airport management reports) has 23,968,186 for 2024, as does Wikipedia's infobox, and 23,313,311 for 2018, so the old figure was also off.
